NJ-2026-S693.title: Prohibits municipalities from requiring certain plan approval related to addition of up to five van accessible parking spaces to existing parking facilities.

actions.text: Assembly Floor Amendment Passed (Quijano) (Voice)
Reported out of Assembly Committee, 2nd Reading
Passed by the Senate (36-0)
Received in the Assembly, Referred to Assembly State and Local Government Committee
Reported from Senate Committee, 2nd Reading
Introduced in the Senate, Referred to Senate Community and Urban Affairs Committee

NJ-2026-S693.aiSummary: Municipalities would not be able to require certain plan approvals for a change that only adds up to five van-accessible parking spaces to an existing parking lot or parking structure in a commercial zone. The rule would apply only when the added spaces meet federal accessibility standards and do not reduce the number of parking spaces required in the original plan. It would take effect right away.

NJ-2026-AR161.title: Recognizes Italian-American Heritage Month and accomplishments and contributions of Italian Americans to NJ and US.

actions.text: Introduced, 1st Reading without Reference, 2nd Reading
Resolution Passed Assembly (78-0-0)
Filed with Secretary of State

NJ-2026-AR161.aiSummary: The resolution recognizes October as Italian-American Heritage Month in New Jersey. It honors the accomplishments and contributions of Italian Americans to the state and the United States, including in science, business, the arts, sports, public service, and military service. The Assembly passed it and it was filed with the Secretary of State.

NJ-2026-A5737.title: Requires DOBI to conduct audits concerning payments made to pharmacy benefits managers and affiliates by pharmaceutical manufacturers.

actions.text: Introduced, Referred to Assembly Financial Institutions and Insurance Committee

NJ-2026-A5737.aiSummary: The bill would require the New Jersey Department of Banking and Insurance to audit payments from drug makers to pharmacy benefits managers and their affiliates. The audited pharmacy benefits manager would pay for the audit and would have 30 days to turn over requested records. If it does not provide the records on time, it could face daily fines of $1,000 to $10,000. The bill would take effect on the first day of the fourth month after it is signed into law.

NJ-2026-A5732.title: Provides subsidy for purchase of health insurance for certain individuals living with type 1 diabetes.

actions.text: Introduced, Referred to Assembly Financial Institutions and Insurance Committee

NJ-2026-A5732.aiSummary: This bill would give an extra subsidy for health insurance bought on the state exchange for households with income below 400 percent of the federal poverty level when someone in the home has type 1 diabetes. The money would come from the Health Insurance Affordability Fund, which is already used to help make individual health coverage more affordable. The act would take effect immediately.

NJ-2026-A5728.title: Requires automatic voter registration processes when applying for concealed carry gun permits.

actions.text: Introduced, Referred to Assembly Judiciary Committee

NJ-2026-A5728.aiSummary: The bill would add voter registration at the same time people apply for a concealed carry handgun permit through local police or the State Police. It would let eligible applicants register to vote, update their voter info, or decline automatic registration. The law would take effect on January 1 after it is enacted.

NJ-2026-A5723.title: Directs Department of Treasury to transfer to DEP as surplus property certain land and improvements thereon in Township of Wall, County of Monmouth.

actions.text: Introduced, Referred to Assembly State and Local Government Committee

NJ-2026-A5723.aiSummary: The bill would have the Treasury Department transfer the state’s interest in the Arthur Brisbane Child Treatment Center property in Wall Township to the Department of Environmental Protection. The land is about 386 acres and includes a main house, two cottages, and a school building. The Parks and Forestry division would be in charge, and the property would be kept as open space. It would take effect right away.

NJ-2026-A5719.title: Requires Office of Special Education in DOE to determine compensatory education services in certain circumstances.

actions.text: Introduced, Referred to Assembly Education Committee

NJ-2026-A5719.aiSummary: The bill would require the Office of Special Education in the Department of Education, or an independent investigator in some cases, to decide what help a student should get after a State complaint finds the student was denied a free appropriate public education. If compensatory education services are needed, the office would set the amount and type of services, while the student’s IEP team would decide how and when they are provided. It would take effect right away and first apply to the next full school year after it is signed into law.

NJ-2026-A5714.title: Authorizes licensed third-party permit professionals to issue certain permits at discretion of DOT.

actions.text: Introduced, Referred to Assembly Transportation and Independent Authorities Committee

NJ-2026-A5714.aiSummary: The bill would let the Department of Transportation use licensed third-party permit professionals to review and approve certain access permits for State highways, if the department chooses. It would set up a licensing program for these professionals and give them 90 days to act on a complete permit application. It affects people and developers seeking permits to build or open driveways, streets, or highways that connect to a State highway.

NJ-2026-A425.title: Increases penalties for certain prohibited sales of tobacco and vapor products.

actions.text: Passed by the Assembly (67-6-5)
Reported out of Assembly Comm. with Amendments, 2nd Reading
Reported and Referred to Assembly Appropriations Committee
Introduced, Referred to Assembly Health Committee

NJ-2026-A425.aiSummary: The bill would raise fines for retailers that sell tobacco products to people under 21. It would also require license suspension after a violation, and license revocation after a second or later violation, with a way for people to report violations anonymously. The new rules would take effect 180 days after enactment.

NJ-2026-A2762.title: Directs Department of Agriculture to advertise and promote New Jersey liquors, beers, and wines.*

actions.text: Assembly Floor Amendment Passed (Quijano) (Voice)
Reported out of Assembly Comm. with Amendments, 2nd Reading
Introduced, Referred to Assembly Agriculture and Natural Resources Committee

NJ-2026-A2762.aiSummary: The bill would direct the New Jersey Department of Agriculture to promote New Jersey-made liquor, beer, and wine. It also would add a broader meaning of “wine product” to include fermented drinks made from fruits and other approved ingredients, not just grapes. The department would have to consult people in the wine, beer, and liquor industries when it sets up a quality rating system for alcohol products.

NJ-2026-A2163.title: Requires Commission on Human Trafficking to post public awareness signage in additional establishments.

actions.text: Passed by the Assembly (77-0-0)
Reported out of Assembly Committee, 2nd Reading
Transferred to Assembly Transportation and Independent Authorities Committee
Reported and Referred to Assembly Appropriations Committee
Introduced, Referred to Assembly Public Safety and Preparedness Committee

NJ-2026-A2163.aiSummary: The bill would require the state human trafficking commission to post public warning signs in more places, including nail salons and Motor Vehicle Commission offices, and it keeps the signs required in other listed businesses and public places. The signs would have to be in English and Spanish and include the human trafficking hotline. Businesses that do not post or replace a missing or damaged sign could face a $300 fine for a first offense and $1,000 for later offenses.

NJ-2026-A1821.title: Prohibits health insurance carriers from denying coverage of nonopioid prescription drugs in favor of opioid prescription drugs.

actions.text: Passed by the Assembly (75-0-1)
Reported out of Assembly Committee, 2nd Reading
Reported and Referred to Assembly Appropriations Committee
Introduced, Referred to Assembly Financial Institutions and Insurance Committee

NJ-2026-A1821.aiSummary: Health insurance carriers would not be allowed to deny coverage for a nonopioid prescription drug just to favor an opioid drug, or make a patient try an opioid first, when a doctor prescribes the nonopioid drug for acute pain. Carriers that keep a drug list would have to avoid treating approved nonopioid pain drugs worse than opioid or narcotic pain drugs in coverage or cost sharing. The same rule would also apply to certain state employee health plans and Medicaid.
